deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 73–74 of the 1981 'topos stratifié' notes). X is a space stratified by a finite poset I, with closed pieces X_i. For a crible (sieve) I' ⊂ I, X_{I'} is the corresponding closed union of strata. The 'elementary topoi' of the stratification are the strata X_i^* together with neighbourhood data U_{ij}, U_{ij}^* (tubular-type neighbourhoods and their deleted versions) for pairs i<j with j a successor of i. These presumably feed a 'gluing/descent' description of the stratified topos as a diagram of type Ĩ.

On the previous page Grothendieck takes two cribles I'' ⊂ I' ⊂ I. This gives the open subset U_{I',I''} = X_{I'} \ X_{I''} of X_{I'}, which carries an induced stratification of type I' \ I''. Its closed pieces are X_{i'} \ (X_{i'} ∩ X_{I''}).

This page continues. For each pair (i',j') with i' ∈ I' \ I'' and j' a successor of i', one has the neighbourhood objects computed inside the open set (subscript X') and those computed in the ambient space. They form the commutative square (17) of inclusions V_{i'j',X'} ↪ V_{i'j'} and V*_{i'j',X'} ↪ V*_{i'j'}, with vertical inclusions V* ⊂ V.

The natural question is whether these restriction inclusions are homotopy equivalences. In other words: do the local homotopy invariants (links / deleted neighbourhoods) of the stratification restrict well to an open union of strata? Grothendieck notes that this is not clear in general. He decides not to worry about comparing the constructions on X_{I'} and on U_{I',I''}, and postpones the verifications of what happens on passing to such an open set.

He then opens section c), 'Les V^{I'''}_{I',I''}'. Cribles are given with I' ⊂ I'' ⊂ I and I''' ⊂ I'' (diagram (18)). Hence there are closed inclusions X_{I'} ⊂ X_{I''} ↪ X_I = X and X_{I'''} ⊂ X_{I''} (diagram (19)). The aim is presumably to define neighbourhood objects V^{I'''}_{I',I''} indexed by pairs or triples of cribles, generalizing the V_{ij} from pairs of strata to pairs of closed unions of strata. The page, which is the last of the folder, breaks off there.
errors: No mathematical error. Grothendieck explicitly flags a gap: whether the inclusions in (17) are homotopy equivalences is 'pas clair en général', and he defers it. With arbitrarily chosen neighbourhoods this can indeed fail without extra hypotheses (e.g. conical / regular neighbourhood conditions). With intrinsic homotopy links (Quinn's holinks) restriction to an open union of strata is automatic.
Section c) is begun but not developed: the notes end on this page.

ideas.what: Restricting a stratification to the open complement U_{I',I''} = X_{I'} \ X_{I''} of a closed union of strata, with induced stratification indexed by I' \ I''
ideas.modern_name: Restriction of a poset-stratified space to an open (upward-closed) sub-poset; open union of strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Thom–Mather, Goresky–MacPherson, Lurie HA App. A)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 discusses 'théorie des multiplicités modérées' / stratified structures only informally

ideas.what: Comparison square (17) between neighbourhood/deleted-neighbourhood data computed in the open subspace vs. in the ambient space; question whether they are homotopy equivalences
ideas.modern_name: Locality/invariance of homotopy links (holinks) under restriction to open subsets
ideas.usually_credited_to: F. Quinn (homotopically stratified sets, 1988); also Siebenmann, Hughes

ideas.what: Neighbourhood objects V^{I'''}_{I',I''} indexed by several cribles (closed unions of strata), generalizing pairwise links to links of closed unions of strata
ideas.modern_name: Generalized/iterated homotopy links indexed by chains of strata; exit-path ∞-category data (multi-step links)

missed.claim: Grothendieck began a systematic definition of neighbourhood objects V^{I'''}_{I',I''} attached to configurations of cribles I'⊂I''⊂I, I'''⊂I''. These would be links of closed unions of strata rather than of single strata. The construction is not carried out: the notes stop here. Modern theory (iterated holinks, exit-path ∞-categories) covers this ground, so the novelty is mainly historical.
missed.quote: c) Les V^{I'''}_{I',I''}. On suppose donnés des cribles (18) I' ⊂ I'' ⊂ I, I''' ⊂ I''
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historically, this documents Grothendieck in 1981 trying to encode a stratified space as a diagram of 'elementary topoi' (strata plus links) indexed by a category built from the stratifying poset. That anticipates the exit-path / stratified homotopy hypothesis programme, but the page itself contains no finished result.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine technical page: a compatibility square, an acknowledged unresolved homotopy-equivalence question, and the start of a new section that is never developed. Its interest is purely historical, as evidence of Grothendieck's 1981 stratified-topos programme anticipating exit-path ideas.
transcription_corrections: Line 'U_{I',I''} = X_{I'} \cap X_{I''}' should read 'U_{I',I''} = X_{I'} \ X_{I''}' (set difference), consistent with (15) on the previous page.
'On suppose donnés des drapeaux[?]' should read 'On suppose donnés des cribles'.
'il faut mieux' should read 'il vaut mieux'.
'que ce soit seulement des équivalences d'homotopie' should read roughly 'que ce soient des équivalences d'homotopie' ('seulement' is an uncertain interlinear insertion).
'en quoi ce passe en s'induisant' should read 'de ce qui se passe en s'induisant ainsi sur un ouvert U_{I',I''}'.
In (19) the second line is X_{I'''} ↪ X_{I''}, written below X_{I'} ⊂ X_{I''} ↪ X_I = X, mirroring diagram (18).
